sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Programmatic Real-Time Ad Exchange and SSP Platform

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Canada-United States Tax Convention (1980), as amended

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, and Regulations SOR/2002-184; Alberta Business Corporations Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. B-9, as amended with beneficial ownership transparency requirements; FINTRAC guidance applicable to non-regulated entities acting as reporting entities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified True Copy of Passport / National Identity Card of each Authorized Signatory and each Individual with Significant Control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public / Competent Commissioner in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (for Hague Convention states) or Consular Legalization (for non-Convention states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Existence for Foreign Corporate Shareholder (if applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company Registry of the jurisdiction of incorporation of the foreign shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign Corporate Board Resolution Authorizing the Incorporation and Appointing Directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate Secretary / Notary of the foreign parent corporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for Incorporation Agent / Local Representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the jurisdiction of execution

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, individuals with significant control, and authorized signatories against OSFI consolidated PEP lists, Global Affairs Canada sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, the UN Security Council consolidated list, the OFAC SDN list, and INTERPOL notices. Enhanced due diligence is required for foreign PEPs and their family members and close associates. Continuous transaction monitoring obligations apply under PCMLTFA and FINTRAC guidance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (CORES) via Service Alberta / authorized Registry Agents; NUANS Name Search Report must be filed through a Registry Agent.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in English or French, and must be distinctive so as not to be confusing with existing names on the NUANS database. If a proposed name includes characters from a non-Canadian language, a phonetically compatible English or French transliteration must be filed, and the legal element must be either 'Unlimited' or 'ULC' for an Alberta unlimited liability corporation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is rejected, the applicant may file a Request for Reconsideration of Name Search Decision with the Director of Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, through the CORES portal or in writing within 30 calendar days of the rejection notice. The request must cite the relevant provision of the Business Corporations Act, address the reasons for confusion or non-distinctiveness, and include, if practicable, an amended distinctive element. If the administrative appeal is unsuccessful, a new name reservation may be submitted with a revised name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for an Alberta ULC engaged in programmatic advertising, provided the arrangement maintains a physical street address in Alberta and a registered agent is available at that address during normal business hours. No statutory requirement mandates a local physical desk, staff, or equipment for a purely digital AdTech platform.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 2-5% annual probability for a low AML-risk ISIC 7310 entity. The Alberta Corporate Registry and Canada Revenue Agency may make verification visits in response to inconsistent filings or compliance red flags, but no routine unannounced on-site inspection regime exists for this industry.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NUANS Name Search Report and Name Reservation Filing (CORES)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry / authorized Registry Agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee plus agent service charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name Clearance and ULC Legal Structure Memorandum
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed professional fee (market benchmark for ULC incorporation review)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO, PEP, OFAC, UN and Domestic Sanctions Background Screening of Directors and Individual Shareholders
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML compliance service provider / legal counsel

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and Apostille / Consular Legalization of Foreign Corporate and Identity Documents
Registered Agent Appointment and Virtual Registered Office Booking (first year, prepaid)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered agent / virtual office service provider

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss 6-10, 101, 122-141, 163
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The ABCA imposes no minimum paid-up capital requirement for an Alberta ULC; shares may be issued without par value, and no escrow account or capital deposition is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. That the Articles of Incorporation of the Unlimited Liability Corporation previously submitted to the Alberta Corporate Registry are ratified and adopted. 2. That the share subscription ledger is approved as filed; all issued common shares are accepted, and consideration received is acknowledged as satisfying the subscription obligations. 3. That the registered office is established at the address identified in the Articles; the corporate records, seal, and statutory registers shall be maintained there with the Corporation's registrar. 4. That the following appointments are confirmed: President and Chief Executive Officer, Corporate Secretary, and Chief Financial Officer, with full authority to open bank accounts, execute agreements, and file statutory returns for the Corporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry through an authorized NUANS service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a proposed corporate name to obtain a NUANS Name Search Report, which is valid for 90 days and must accompany the Articles of Incorporation. Verify that the name is distinctive and does not conflict with existing registered names or trademarks in Alberta.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is flagged as confusingly similar, file a revised name with a fresh NUANS report or submit a written consent from the conflicting name holder for reconsideration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Articles of Incorporation and Receipt of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (electronic or paper filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 (Articles of Incorporation) specifying the corporate name, registered office address, share structure, first directors, and any restrictions on business. Submit the form electronically through the Corporate Registry system or by mail/courier. Upon approval, the Registry issues a Certificate of Incorporation with a unique Alberta Corporate Access Number.
required_dossiers: Form 1 - Articles of Incorporation (signed by incorporator)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a notice of defect or requests additional information, the incorporator may cure the deficiency by amending Form 1 and re-filing within 30 days; rejected applications receive a written explanation and refund of fees less administrative charges.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Organizational Meeting, Registered Office Adoption, and Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: First directors of the corporation (internal governance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the organizational meeting and adopt the First Board Resolution approving share subscriptions, ratifying the registered office address, adopting by-laws, and appointing officers. Prepare the minute book, corporate registers, share certificates, and corporate seal.
required_dossiers: Share subscription agreements and share certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an appointed officer or director declines to act, the board may appoint a replacement by ordinary resolution; a change of registered office may be effected by filing Form 3 - Notice of Change of Registered Office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Canada Revenue Agency (Business Number and Tax Accounts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, obtain a 9-digit Business Number by filing Form RC1 or through the CRA's online Business Registration service. Register the corporation income tax account, GST/HST account, and payroll deductions account as applicable to the AdTech platform's revenue streams.
required_dossiers: RC1 - Request for a Business Number and Tax Accounts
Identification of Canadian directors and signing officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA queries the application, correct the legal name or address, re-submit RC1, or contact the CRA Business Window; processing resumes within 5 business days of clarification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Provincial Annual Return and Municipal Business Licensing Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry and applicable municipal authority (e.g., City of Calgary or City of Edmonton)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Alberta Annual Return within 60 days after each anniversary of incorporation. If physical office premises are established, obtain a municipal business licence and confirm zoning and commercial occupancy permits.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late Annual Returns may be cured with an amended filing and late fee; revoked municipal licences may be reinstated upon proof of zoning compliance and payment of outstanding penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable; ISIC 7310 (NAICS 541810) is a digital services activity. No Alberta industrial manufacturing licence is required. Alberta Municipal Affairs governs building and fire safety for office premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required - no industrial operating licence applicable; only a municipal business licence for physical office premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - office-based digital services with no point-source discharge; no EIA registration or full assessment required under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (EPEA).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste release thresholds apply. Standard municipal waste and e-waste disposal rules apply; any HVAC or refrigerant maintenance must comply with the Alberta Ozone-depleting Substances Regulation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Alberta Fire Code compliance (fire safety inspection and certification for commercial occupancy), municipal building occupancy permit, and Occupational Health and Safety Code compliance (workplace hazard assessment, training, and first-aid requirements) under the OHS Act of Alberta.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); full administrative authority for federal corporate income tax and federal GST through My Business Account and Business Registration Online (BRO) portal; Alberta corporate income tax is administered by the CRA on behalf of the Province of Alberta under the Tax Collection Agreement, with Alberta Tax and Revenue Administration retaining audit and assessment oversight for provincial taxpayer services
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Alberta ULC obtains a federal Business Number (BN) with a separate GST/HST program account by submitting Form RC1 through CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) or by paper filing; the non-resident shareholder or ULC must appoint a representative for service of process and returns using Form RC59 and must maintain books and records in Canada; issuance of the BN and GST/HST account is generally completed within one to two business days, and the BN constitutes the single statutory TIN for CRA and Alberta corporate tax filings; no separate provincial tax registration identification is required
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Under US Treasury Regulation Section 301.7701-2(b)(8), an Alberta unlimited liability corporation is not a per se corporation and is an eligible entity; a US parent may file an IRS Form 8832 check-the-box election to treat the ULC as a disregarded entity for US federal tax purposes; CRA administrative policy permits a qualifying single-shareholder ULC owned by a US corporation to be recognized on a look-through basis with the US shareholder treated as carrying on business in Canada, subject to the ULC filing Canadian Part I returns and maintaining arm's length accounts; draft hybrid mismatch proposals (Income Tax Act sections 17.1 et seq., issued as draft legislation but not yet enacted) would disallow double-deduction or deduction-without-inclusion outcomes arising from hybrid entity classification, and no elective safe harbor for such hybrid structures is currently available

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) - federal value-added tax under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act; Alberta has no Provincial Sales Tax (PST) and no Harmonized Sales Tax (HST), resulting in the sole application of the 5% federal GST to taxable supplies made in Alberta
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in annual worldwide gross revenues from taxable supplies in Canada (the small-supplier threshold); a person must register for GST once this threshold is exceeded in a calendar quarter; special deemed-registration rules under Excise Tax Act subsections 240(1.1) to 240(1.4) apply to non-resident suppliers soliciting orders for goods to be delivered in Canada, which can remove the small-supplier exemption even below the CAD 30,000 threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, API clearance, or digital stamping regime is currently in force in Canada; the Pan-Canadian E-Invoicing Framework, which is Peppol-compliant, is voluntary and is being phased in for federal procurement only; GST/HST registrants are required to file returns electronically via GST/HST NETFILE and CRA requires taxpayers to preserve books and records in a readable, machine-accessible electronic format for audit purposes

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Programmatic advertising, ad exchange, DSP and SSP services supplied to non-resident recipients are zero-rated under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act (ETA): the general rule for services supplied to non-resident persons (ETA Schedule VI, Part V, section 7) applies where the recipient is a non-resident at the time the tax becomes payable and the supply is not in respect of Canadian real property, tangible personal property situated in Canada, or intangibles to be used or enjoyed in Canada; the advertising-specific provision (ETA Schedule VI, Part V, section 10) supports zero-rating of advertising services directed to persons outside Canada; tangible goods exported from Canada are zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, sections 20 and 21 provided export shipment and customs documentation are retained; the supplier must substantiate the non-resident status of the recipient and the foreign destination in contemporaneous books and records to support input tax credit claims and refunds; although Canadian legislation imposes no statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline, a 180-day documentary collection benchmark is applied in CRA audit practice to evidence that the export was a genuine cross-border commercial transaction
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA Form B13A or approved electronic EDI/ACI transmission) evidencing physical exportation of goods from Canada
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / proof of delivery together with commercial invoice and the programmatic or ad-server contract evidencing the non-resident recipient for zero-rated services
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank wire confirmation and foreign exchange documentation evidencing receipt of export proceeds from the non-resident counterparty
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may deny zero-rating where the exporter fails to retain the complete statutory documentation bundle, reassessing the full GST as if the supply were standard-rated and collecting the under-remitted tax with compound/arrears interest; the four-year normal reassessment period is reopened without time limitation where a misrepresentation attributable to neglect, carelessness, wilful default, or fraud is established; civil penalties apply under ETA section 285 for false statements in returns (up to 25% of net tax claimed in the false return), and gross negligence penalties may be imposed under income tax provisions where the same transactions affect Part I liability; wilful evasion constitutes a criminal offence under ETA section 327 punishable by fines of up to twice the amount of tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment for up to five years

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); foreign exchange regulatory coordination is distributed among the Department of Finance Canada, the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI), the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC), and the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current and capital account convertibility under IMF Article VIII. There are no general foreign exchange controls, no exchange allocation system, and no administrative pre-clearance for inward or outward remittances. Profit repatriation is legally unrestricted, but dividends must be declared out of distributable profits under corporate law, and non-resident dividend/remittance payments are subject to Part XIII withholding tax (default 25%, reduced by tax treaty if applicable). Capital inflows remain subject to the Investment Canada Act net-benefit review only when statutory thresholds are exceeded.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Export proceeds may be retained freely in Canadian dollars or foreign currency. Only normal reporting duties apply, such as customs export declarations, balance-of-payments reporting to Statistics Canada, and FINTRAC cross-border electronic funds transfer reporting for transactions at or above CAD 10,000.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Low for primary treasury and escrow use. An offshore electronic money institution (EMI) cannot obtain a Canadian bank license, cannot become a direct participant in Payments Canada settlement systems, and cannot offer insured deposits. It may be engaged only as a supplementary low-value payment facilitator, subject to the Retail Payment Activities Act registration and restrictions on holding Canadian end-customer funds. A fully regulated Canadian bank remains mandatory for the ULC’s core liquidity and compliance infrastructure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors need not appear physically in all cases. Canadian chartered banks permit remote onboarding using live video verification, notarized identification packages, corporate registry searches, and beneficial-ownership validation. For a non-resident owned ULC, Canadian banks commonly require at least one principal director or authorized officer to complete a video interview; a branch visit may be waived if enhanced due diligence, credit assessment, and independent background checks are satisfactory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership concentration, especially the ULC’s unlimited liability corporate form with foreign controlling shareholders, triggers enhanced due diligence and may prompt refusal by risk-adverse onboarding units.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Alberta corporate registry extract, certificate of continuous record, articles of association notice of unlimited liability, register of directors and shareholders, ultimate beneficial ownership declaration, source-of-wealth evidence for each contributor, prior bank reference letter, and audited or reviewed financial statements for the most recent fiscal period.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity programmatic advertising flows through the AdTech exchange platform may appear as numerous same-day cross-border electronic fund transfers to publishers, DSPs, and SSPs, creating a typology risk of layering or unlicensed money services activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed flow-of-funds diagram, executed agreements with publishers and platform counterparts, payment settlement whitelist, contractual payment waterfall, sanctions and FATF screening logs, transaction monitoring policy, periodic independent AML audit reports, and written confirmation that the ULC only settles verifiable programmatic media transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlimited Liability Corporation pass-through tax election and potential fiscal transparency can be misunderstood as an indication of undisclosed beneficiaries or artificial loss-making structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent Canadian and United States tax opinions confirming the ULC’s tax classification and any check-the-box elections, capital account statements for each shareholder, comprehensive shareholder register, board resolutions approving capital contributions, and multi-year cash-flow models supporting commercial substance and economic activity in Alberta.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border shareholder loans, dividend declarations, and management fees may trigger anti-profit-stripping red flags or suspicion of unauthorized capital repatriation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transfer pricing documentation for intercompany services, board-approved distribution minutes, dividend solvency certificates, treaty residency certificates for non-Canadian shareholders, CRA T5/T106 reporting substantiation, annotated bank statements showing the commercial rationale of each remittance, and a treasury policy defining arm’s length funding and liquidity thresholds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity and shareholder loan contributions are received via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 from the foreign parent or investor into the ULC’s Canadian operational account. The payment must reference the ULC corporate name and the intended purpose code for capital contribution or intercompany funding. Supporting onboarding evidence includes a certified board resolution authorizing the capital injection, proof of shareholder identity, source-of-funds documentation, and a contemporaneous capitalization table. FINTRAC cross-border electronic funds transfer reporting applies at or above CAD 10,000, and if the controlling share acquisition exceeds Investment Canada Act thresholds, a net-benefit notification or application may be required. No exchange control approval is required for the conversion of foreign currency into Canadian dollars.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for the programmatic ad inventory, publisher payments, data license fees, platform charges, and operational vendor costs are executed through SWIFT MT103 for priority cross-border wires, commercial letters of credit for contractually documented goods or services requiring documentary settlement, and MT700-series messages for LC issuance. Domestic disbursements clear through Payments Canada LYNX for high-value real-time wires or through the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) and ACH Direct for batch settlement. Each disbursement must pass sanctions screening, beneficiary bank verification, and transaction-purpose documentation to satisfy FINTRAC and OSFI expectations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards traded with a regulated Canadian chartered bank or CIRO-authorized dealer
FX swaps and cross-currency swaps for balance-sheet hedging of intercompany loans and capital contributions
Vanilla FX call and put options purchased through an OSFI-supervised or CIRO-member counterparty
Limited-use non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) where the underlying payment currency is not actively deliverable in the Canadian interbank market
Interest-rate and cross-currency basis swaps when legally matched to a specific foreign-currency liability

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for AdTech platform operations. Available incentives: federal SR&ED investment tax credit (15%-35% depending on CCPC status), Alberta Innovation Tax Credit (30% refundable for qualifying investments), and reduced small business rates (federal 9% + Alberta 2%) on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income if the ULC qualifies as a Canadian-controlled private corporation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; electronic filing through CRA Corporation Internet Filing (CIF) or CRA My Business Account portal. Alberta corporate income tax is not reported on a separate AT1 return; the provincial tax is integrated with the federal T2 under the federal-provincial tax collection agreement.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after the fiscal year-end. Example: December 31 year-end is due June 30. Interim instalments are payable on a prescribed schedule where tax exceeds CAD 3,000.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income for the year after applying carryforwards, deductions, and loss offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Canadian-source taxable income. Where the ULC is owned by non-residents, bracket shareholder losses or treaty-protected income may require Schedules 7, 91, and Form T1091.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax computed at 15% general rate or 9% small business rate before credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the federal-provincial abatement and any treaty-based exemption, such as income attributable to a foreign permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alberta provincial tax computed at 8% general rate or 2% small business rate on Alberta-allocated income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident ULC without a permanent establishment in Alberta, Alberta tax generally does not apply; apportionment is made using the T2 provincial allocation schedules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty is 5% of the balance due plus 1% per full month of delinquency up to 12 months. Daily prescribed interest accrues on unpaid balances. Failure to file Form T106 triggers CAD 100 per day (minimum CAD 1,000, maximum CAD 25,000).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T106 Information Return of Non-Arm's Length Transactions; filed with the T2 via CRA e-services or CRA Rag-Mail.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same due date as the T2 return: six months after fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identifies the Canadian ULC and each related non-resident party involved in controlled transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide full legal name, country of residence, tax identification number, and nature of the non-resident relationship.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate fair market value of all non-arm's length transactions, classified by type (goods, services, royalties, interest, dividends).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the transfer-pricing method selected and supply comparable benchmarks. Ensure amounts are reported in Canadian dollars.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Same T106 penalty regime as above: CAD 100 per day, subject to CAD 25,000 cap; T106 penalties are separate from T2 late filing penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding tax on dividends paid by a Canadian ULC to non-resident shareholders
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain treaty-reduced withholding, the non-resident shareholder must complete and deliver Form NR301 (Declaration of Facts for Withholding Tax Exemption or Reduction) plus a valid Certificate of Residence (TRC) from its home jurisdiction before each dividend payment. The payer reviews the form, withholds at the treaty rate, and files Form NR4 with CRA. A TRC issued by the foreign authority is the primary administrative evidence of residence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate: 25% on gross IP royalties and debt interest. Under the Canada-US DTA: arm's-length non-participating interest is generally 0%; royalties for patents, trademarks, and know-how are generally reduced to 10%; other treaty rates range from 10% to 15% depending on the partner jurisdiction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 aggregate gross fair market value of controlled non-arm's-length cross-border transactions in a taxation year triggers mandatory contemporaneous Local File documentation. Country-by-Country Report and Master File requirements apply to MNE groups with consolidated global revenue exceeding CAD 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not maintain a standalone Economic Substance Regulation regime comparable to the UAE. The CRA applies section 245 GAAR, section 247 transfer-pricing re-characterization, and substance-over-form jurisprudence to disregard arrangements lacking genuine commercial or economic substance. A ULC operating as a programmatic AdTech exchange must demonstrate actual personnel, decision-making, allocation of risk, and revenue-generating activity in Canada to preserve treaty benefits and avoid treaty-shopping challenges under the OECD MLI.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of advertising revenue, fabrication of deductible expenses, or a conscious false statement on a T2 return or NR4 withholding form.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded under section 163(2) ITA; criminal prosecution under section 239(1) ITA carries fines up to CAD 100,000 and imprisonment for up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign, authorize, or acquiesce in false returns are jointly and severally liable for the penalty. Courts may impose travel bans pending investigation and asset seizure orders; personal imprisonment is available for willful evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Late Filing / Non-Filing of Corporate Returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file a T2 for more than six months after the fiscal year-end, especially when combined with unreported NRA or withholding transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 5% late-filing penalty plus 1% per month for up to 12 months, along with daily prescribed interest; persistent non-filing permits a CRA jeopardy assessment (section 152(4)) and revocation of director clearance certificates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be assessed personally under section 227.1 ITA for unremitted source deductions and can be listed for cross-border departure travel prevention orders in flagrant cases of repeated non-compliance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an Albertan ULC solely as a conduit for profit-stripping, dividend routing, or treaty benefit without local staff, contracts, risk-bearing, or substantive board activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR re-determination of all tax consequences with gross negligence penalties and interest; treaty relief may be denied under the Principal Purpose Test (MLI Article 7); provincial authorities may dissolve the ULC for cause.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly maintain a sham ULC may be personally assessed on deemed distributions or adjusted income; the corporate veil can be pierced where funds are mingled with personal accounts, and directors face civil restitution orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Cross-border related-party transactions (fees to parent, IP royalties, intercompany loans) exceeding the CAD 1 million threshold without robust contemporaneous TP documentation or T106 filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 10% penalty under section 247(3) on the net transfer-pricing adjustment amount; additional section 247(7) per-day penalties for deficient records; interest accrues on the resulting assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve transfer pricing without an arm's-length review are personally liable if they knew or ought to have known of mispricing and failed to remedy it; severe cases trigger executive travel bans and criminal money-laundering charges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a programmatic ad exchange with high-volume Swift/ACH flows without registering as a Money Services Business, filing Suspicious Transaction Reports, or conducting client due diligence on DSP/SSP counterparties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative monetary penalties under the PCMLTFA: first violation up to CAD 500,000, subsequent violations up to CAD 1,000,000; criminal money laundering convictions carry imprisonment up to 10 years and asset forfeiture.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers are criminally liable if they consent to or fail to prevent AML violations. Courts may issue personal confiscation orders or travel bans under the Criminal Code, and the corporate veil is waived for fraud and money laundering objectives.
